kanbanData: Storage: ~/.local/share/kanban/board.json (1618 B, last written 16:00 today), shape {version:1, tasks:[{id,title,desc,status:'todo'|'doing'|'done',daily?:templateId}], dailies:[{id,title,desc,times:['HH:MM'],last:ms}]}. Today it holds 11 tasks (6 todo, 1 doing, 4 done) and 1 daily template (times ['08:00']) with one instance on the board. Writer: /home/lyfmt/Projects/my-arch-kit/kanban/shell/Store.qml rewrites the whole file through a FileView with atomicWrites (temp + rename) on every change. A 30 s Timer re-adds daily instances to the top of TODO when a time slot passes. Can another quickshell config read it? Yes: it is a plain JSON file at a fixed path, so a menu can use its own FileView on that path with watchChanges: true and onFileChanged: reload(). Whether watching survives kanban's rename-on-write was not verified. Writing from the menu is unsafe: kanban's FileView has no watchChanges, so it never reloads outside edits and its next save() overwrites them. Its IPC is only toggle/open/close. A menu that marks tasks done would need kanban changes first (watchChanges + reload, or a mutation IPC). Calendar limits: tasks have no due, created or completed dates. The id is Date.now() in base36 plus 4 random chars, so creation time can be decoded, but that is a hack. Dailies only store refresh times and the last refresh. So a calendar page can show 'today' (current TODO/DOING plus daily instances with their HH:MM) but cannot place tasks on other days without a schema change. DMS CalendarService has no backend here, so no other event source exists.
quickbarInterpretation: Most likely reading: the app icons in the top bar's tray cluster. Second: the fixed quick-entry list from the user's own prototypes. A dock is ruled out. The two leading readings overlap enough that one short question to the user settles it. (1) Tray apps on the current top bar. Today these are Feishu, magpie, Fcitx5/Rime, Sunshine and Clash Verge, plus QQ since 16:40. For: the sentence lists menu functions that each match something on the bar (power ↔ control-center POWER/Super+X, 显示数值 ↔ CPU/RAM/battery gauges, 日历 ↔ island date), then says the top-bar items can be deleted. 应用入口 lines up with the only cluster of app icons on the bar. The tray is also where the user actually opens their most-used apps: magpie #1, Feishu #2, Clash Verge #4 and QQ #5 are all in the tray. Against: tray items are running background apps, not launch shortcuts. Fcitx5 and Sunshine are not apps you 'enter'. 快捷栏 is not the usual word for 托盘. Absorbing the tray means the menu must host live SNI items (activate and context menu), and removing systemTray from the bar loses at-a-glance status such as Clash's proxy-state icon. (2) The quick-entry list from the user's prototypes. That means the p3-miku items (APPS/FILES/TERMINAL/BROWSER/MUSIC/KANBAN/CALENDAR/SETTINGS/POWER) or phone v2's APPS page. For: the user's own vocabulary ties 快捷 to these prototypes (p5-reference/index.html calls the phone '快捷手机 · 快捷入口手机的视觉原型'). The user also uses 当前已有的 for a p5-reference prototype in the same message, so 当前 need not mean 'live on the desktop'. The items match real keybinds (Mod+Z/E/T/B/M/;/F2, Super+X). Against: p3-miku already contains these items, so the parenthetical would add nothing. Phone v2's commands are wrong for this machine. (3) The most-used apps from appusage.json (magpie 69, 飞书 67, Buffin 64, Clash Verge 63, QQ 37, Termius 14, ...). For: it is real data, it overlaps (1) heavily, and the launcher already ranks by it. Against: nothing on screen today is a 快捷栏 showing this list, and the Mod+Z carousel already presents apps in this order. (4) A DMS dock or pinned apps. Ruled out: the dock is off and pinnedApps is empty. (5) niri app keybinds (快捷键): kitty, chromium, thunar, music, kanban. The word 'shortcut' fits, but 栏 means a bar, and this set is the same as (2). Suggested question for the user: 应用入口是指顶栏右边托盘里的那几个图标（飞书/喜鹊/Clash/QQ…），还是一组固定的快捷启动项（终端/浏览器/文件/音乐/看板…+常用应用）？ A hybrid answers both: live tray apps plus fixed launch items seeded from the usage top list.

Other findings that affect the plan:
(1) Version mismatch: the installed DMS package is now dux-shell 2.0.0-1 (provides dms-shell=2.0.0, `dms v2.0.0`, installed 2026-10-28). dms-p5 patches target v1.6.3 and build from the cached ~/.local/share/dms-p5/upstream/v1.6.3. The running UI is that 1.6.3-based build (qs -p ~/.local/share/dms-p5/shell, pid 1348). Decide the base before any new dms-p5 patch work.
(2) Deleting bar widgets has these consequences. cpuUsage/memUsage: P5ProcessBoard loses its only entry (Ctrl+Alt+Del opens the stock modal). focusedWindow: P5WindowDossier becomes unreachable. clipboard: P5WantedBoard is still reachable via Mod+Alt+V. controlCenterButton: the control center is still reachable via `control-center` IPC (island first). battery: the stock battery popout is lost. systemTray: the SNI watcher is owned by the DMS qs process (pid 1348). A tray section inside a dms-p5 menu gets the items for free. A separate qs config would have to register as a second host; that was not verified, and neither was whether the watcher stays up once no bar widget uses SystemTray.
(3) dms-p5/AGENTS.md mentions a pull cord (拉绳) on the island, but no code for it exists in any commit. The memory note says the user wanted pull cords.
(4) The island weather group is not shown today (weather unavailable, no location set).
